text:
TwinDesk 

 
 Your Mac, PC, Linux box, Android phone and iPhone, working as one desk. 
 One mouse and keyboard for every computer. Screens, files, clipboard, notifications, cameras, calls and texts, shared. 
 Free and open source. No account, no cloud, and on iPhone not even an app to install. 
 An open-source alternative to Microsoft Phone Link, KDE Connect, Intel Unison and Synergy, in one app.

 What is TwinDesk?

You probably own more than one computer. A work laptop and a gaming PC. A MacBook and the Windows
machine you can't give up. A Linux box under the desk. And a phone that's never more than a metre
away. Each one is great on its own. Together they're a mess: two keyboards, files emailed to
yourself, a phone you keep picking up, the same tab opened three times.

 TwinDesk turns all of them into one desk. 

Push the mouse off the edge of your Mac's screen and it carries on onto the PC, keyboard and all.
Copy on one, paste on the other. Drag a file across the edge and drop it there. Open the PC's apps
in windows on your Mac. Turn a tablet into a second screen. Answer your phone's calls from the
computer, use its camera in your video calls, and drive the computer from the couch with it. Walk to
another device and ReZume brings the tab, the video or the document you were on with you.

It's one app on every computer, so a Mac and a PC pair exactly like two Macs. Phones are full peers,
not notification mirrors. And an iPhone, an iPad or any device with a browser joins by typing
 twindesk.local .

 Looking for a Phone Link alternative? TwinDesk does what Microsoft Phone Link does (texts, calls,
notifications, photos and your phone's screen and apps on the computer), and it also works on a Mac
and on Linux, with an iPhone as well as Android, and without a Microsoft account. It replaces KDE
Connect and Intel Unison the same way. See how it compares.

 
 
 

 🔀 Any combination 
Mac, Windows, Linux, Android, iPhone, iPad and any browser, two at a time or all at once.

 
 

 📡 Anywhere 
Same Wi-Fi, a USB cable, Tailscale, or no shared network at all: Bluetooth and a direct Wi-Fi link.

 
 

 🔒 Yours alone 
No account, no cloud, no telemetry. Devices talk only to each other, end-to-end encrypted.

 
 

 ⚡ Built for speed 
A native Rust input lane over UDP, a parallel file engine, hardware video. How.

 Portable runs without installing ( ARM64 ). Full KVM : x64 · ARM64 

 
 

 🐧 Linux X11 and Wayland, x86 64 

 
 
 
 
 NixOS: nix run github:InukaAsith/TwinDesk ( more ) Full KVM : .deb · AppImage 

 
 

 🤖 Android 10 or later, phones and tablets 

 
 
 The full app adds notifications, texts and Accessibility; the computer can install it for you 

 
 

 📱 iPhone and iPad iOS 16 or later 

 
 
 

 
 
 

 

 🍺 Homebrew on macOS: brew install --cask inukaasith/twindesk/twindesk 
 Update with brew upgrade --cask twindesk : TwinDesk opens again by itself if it was running, so a Mac you drive only through it gets its mouse back. The tap follows every release. 

 

 🐧 APT on Debian, Ubuntu, Mint and Pop! OS, kept up to date by apt upgrade : 

 

 The repository follows every release within a few hours. 

 Already installed? Install now in the app updates it in place, with your edition's file (Portable stays Portable, Full KVM stays Full KVM). Update every device you pair: a newer TwinDesk still talks to an older one, and a new feature switches on when both sides have it. 
Every file and older version is on the releases page . 

 

 
 ⚠️ First launch: the apps aren't code-signed how to allow them on macOS, Windows, Android and iPhone 

TwinDesk is free and has no paid Apple Developer ID or Windows code-signing certificate, so
macOS and Windows don't know who made it and ask once before opening it. The source is all here.

 🍎 macOS 

The easiest way is Homebrew , which installs it ready to open:
 brew install --cask inukaasith/twindesk/twindesk 

From the .dmg instead:

1. Drag TwinDesk into Applications and open it. macOS says it can't verify TwinDesk: click Done 
 (not Move to Bin).
2. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security , scroll down to Security and click Open Anyway 
 next to "TwinDesk was blocked". Enter your password, then click Open Anyway again.

You do this once; updates open normally. If macOS says TwinDesk is damaged and can't be
opened , it isn't: run this in Terminal, then open it again:

 

 🪟 Windows 

1. If the browser warns that the file isn't commonly downloaded, choose Keep (in Edge: ⋯ ›
 Keep › Show more › Keep anyway ).
2. When the installer shows Windows protected your PC (SmartScreen), click More info , then
 Run anyway .

On Windows 11 with Smart App Control on, unsigned apps are blocked with no Run anyway button.
The only way past it is turning it off (Windows Security › App & browser control › Smart App Control
settings), and on many Windows 11 versions it can't be turned back on without reinstalling Windows.

 🤖 Android 

1. Open the downloaded .apk. Android asks to allow your browser or Files app to install unknown
 apps : tap Settings , turn on Allow from this source , go back and tap Install .
2. If Play Protect warns about an unrecognised developer, tap More details › Install anyway .

The full app (notifications, texts and Accessibility) is easiest installed by the computer over
wireless debugging (Phone page › Notifications from the phone): Android then

install.title: Install it
install.html:
TwinDesk isn't on the App Store yet (that's what sponsoring pays for), so you install the IPA with your own Apple ID:


  1. Install AltStore or SideStore on the iPhone.
  2. Tap Add to AltStore (or SideStore) above on the iPhone, or add this source by hand:
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/InukaAsith/TwinDesk/main/altstore.json
  3. Install TwinDesk from the source. It updates from there when a new version is out.

With a free Apple ID, apps installed this way have to be refreshed every 7 days; AltStore and SideStore do it for you in the background. Needs iOS or iPadOS 16 or later.

Or let the computer do it (new in 3.2, opt in): the TwinDesk iPhone page on Mac, Windows or Linux signs the app with your own free Apple ID, installs it over the cable or Wi-Fi and refreshes it before it expires. Updates install the same way.
